lead_headline: Chick-fil-A debuts Colorado's first drive-thru-only format at Central Park as $6.1M Douglas County estate enters foreclosure

restaurant.blurb: 3 new leads today: 7-Eleven convenience store (Federal Blvd closure), Samir Mediterranean/Afghan (Congress Park opening unclear), and Taqueria La Morenas (Harvey Park temp closure). Active pipeline: 116 leads (59 openings, 57 closures).

foreclosure.blurb: $6.1M Douglas County property at 18901 Longs Way stands as the week's sole $4M+ filing — a scheduled auction Thursday alongside 51 smaller properties.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today extends Monday's filing drought into day two — the longest quiet spell since February. This week's 20-application volume holds at double the pre-March baseline, led by restaurant/tavern expansions in Westminster (Red Lotus Den food hall), Overland (The Couloir après bar), and Regis (Ultra Lounge West karaoke bar). The sustained pace suggests State licensing capacity remains clear despite elevated demand, though Tuesday-Thursday typically anchor weekly volume. Zero status changes marks fourth consecutive day without processing updates.

reputation.blurb: Zero mentions yesterday drops the 7-day total to 36 across 9 sources — down 29% from last week's 51-mention baseline and marking the third consecutive weekly decline since mid-April's peak. Instagram (12) maintains weekly dominance ahead of Denver Post (6), Facebook (5), and Reddit (4). The sustained three-week contraction (54→51→36) suggests development news cycle fatigue as major announcements thin heading into late spring. Notable pickups: Mustard's Last Stand closure (Instagram), Denver sapphic bar discussion (Reddit), and outdoor industry networking coverage (Facebook). Week-over-week momentum signals continued cooling despite Instagram's sticky engagement.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +0 yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) holds MTD at +18 (+0.9/day), 90-day net at +141. The 7-day total of +8 (13 new, 5 canceled) marks a sharp 38% drop from last week's +13 performance, driven entirely by acquisition slowdown — new signups fell 50% (13 vs 26) while cancellations improved 62% (5 vs 13). The recent pattern shows Monday-Tuesday flatlines bookending midweek conversion: April 15 spiked +6, then the last four days delivered zero net as both acquisition and churn went dormant. MTD's +0.9/day pace continues trailing YTD's +1.3/day benchmark, but the sustained low-churn environment (just 5 cancellations across 7 days) signals healthier retention fundamentals even as late-month momentum stalls.
